label: prf:knot-factor-spectral-form
title: Proof of knot factor spectral derivation
html:
The e_\lambda are orthogonal central idempotents, so e_\lambda x = x e_\lambda and \chi_\mu(e_\lambda x) = \delta_{\lambda\mu}\,\chi_\lambda(x) for every x \in A. Hence

  \tau(e_\lambda x) \;=\; \sum_\mu y_\mu\, \chi_\mu(e_\lambda x) \;=\; y_\lambda\, \chi_\lambda(x).

With x = \mathbf{1} this gives w_\lambda = \tau(e_\lambda) = y_\lambda d_\lambda, and \sum_\lambda w_\lambda = \tau\bigl(\sum_\lambda e_\lambda\bigr) = \tau(\mathbf{1}) = 1. With x = \beta_\mathcal{K}^* and linearity of \tau,

  \tau\bigl(\pi(\beta_\mathcal{K})\,\beta_\mathcal{K}^*\bigr)
  \;=\; \sum_\lambda \frac{\chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K})}{d_\lambda}\, y_\lambda\, \chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K}^*)
  \;=\; \sum_\lambda w_\lambda\, \frac{\chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K})\,\chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K}^*)}{d_\lambda^{\,2}}.

Since \chi_\lambda(\pi(x)) = \chi_\lambda(x), the same computation with \pi(\beta_\mathcal{K}^*) in place of \beta_\mathcal{K}^* gives the same sum. For \beta_\mathcal{K} = \mathbf{1} every ratio is 1 and the sum is \sum_\lambda w_\lambda = 1. At z = q^3/(q^2+1), y_\lambda = 0 for three-row \lambda, so w_\lambda = 0 there. \square

Scope. The projection \pi is essential. The uncentred entry \tau(\beta_\mathcal{K}\,\beta_\mathcal{K}^*) equals \sum_\lambda y_\lambda\,\chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K}\beta_\mathcal{K}^*), the character of a product, which is not the product of characters unless one factor is central. Weighting that uncentred entry by \dim_q^2 V_\lambda / [n]_q! would at \beta_\mathcal{K} = \mathbf{1} require 1 = \sum_\lambda \dim_q^2 V_\lambda/[n]_q!, which fails for q \neq 1.
